title: European Commission confirms EU Academy data leak
summary: At its midday briefing on 23 November 2026 the European Commission confirmed that the EU Academy e-learning platform was hit by the cyber campaign against the Commission and that personal data of its users, who are external to the EU institutions, leaked; an EU official told POLITICO this includes names and email addresses, and the full scale is still under investigation. Public access to the platform has been disabled, users were told through a notice on the EU Academy website rather than individually, and the European Data Protection Supervisor has been informed. The Commission says the attack used an AI-assisted tool but has not attributed it or said whether it is contained. The Register reports that suspicious activity was first detected on 22 October.
why: Two lessons for tenant owners. Anyone in your organisation who used EU Academy with a work address can expect targeted phishing that borrows EU branding. And the criticism of a website-only notice is a reminder to decide in advance how you would notify people: under GDPR Article 34, a public communication instead of individual notices is only an option when contacting people individually would involve disproportionate effort.
todo: Do now: warn staff who may have registered with EU Academy and add EU Academy and Commission themes to phishing awareness and mail-flow detections.
Review your incident response plan: who decides on notifying data subjects, which channel you use and what you need to show if you choose a public notice.
Follow the Commission's updates; whether the attack is contained is not yet confirmed.
effective_note: Confirmed by the Commission on 23 Nov 2026; investigation ongoing.
